name: LT1962EMS8-5#TRPBF
title: LT1962 series: 300 mA low-noise micropower LDO regulators, fixed and adjustable, in MSOP-8
summary: A family of 300mA low-dropout linear regulators drawing 30µA of quiescent current and under 1µA in shutdown, running from 1.8V to 20V. Dropout is 270mV at full load. A 0.01µF capacitor on the BYP pin brings output noise down to 20µVRMS over 10Hz to 100kHz. Fixed outputs of 1.5V, 1.8V, 2.5V, 3V, 3.3V and 5V and an adjustable 1.22V-to-20V version come in the 8-lead MSOP; the parts are stable with output capacitors from 3.3µF, aluminum electrolytic, tantalum or ceramic and protect themselves against reverse input, reverse output current, overcurrent and overtemperature.
key_figures: 0.27 V typ, 0.33 V max at 300 mA (25 °C)
20 µVRMS, 10 Hz to 100 kHz, CBYP = 0.01 µF
3.3 µF minimum, ESR 3 Ω or less

notes: Every code is the same 8-lead plastic MSOP; they differ in output voltage and grade. E grade is tested at 25°C and guaranteed from 0°C to 125°C, with –40°C performance assured by design and characterization; I grade is guaranteed from –40°C to 125°C (Note 3).
The grade is not in the part marking; a label on the shipping container identifies it.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Regulated output to the load. It needs at least 3.3µF of output capacitance to stay stable; loads with large transient steps need more capacitance to hold down the peaks.

pins.name: SENSE
pins.function: Feedback input to the error amplifier on the fixed versions. Tying it to OUT at the load (Kelvin connection) removes the drop across the PC trace resistance from the regulated voltage, though that drop adds to the dropout voltage. It draws 10µA at the rated output voltage. Taking it negative with respect to ground (for instance when the load returns to a negative rail) does not stop the part starting or regulating.

pins.name: BYP
pins.function: Noise bypass for the internal reference. A capacitor from OUT to BYP lowers output noise; up to 0.01µF may be used, which gives 20µVRMS typical over 10Hz to 100kHz. The pin is clamped inside to ±0.6V (one VBE). Leave it open when no capacitor is fitted.

pins.name: SHDN
pins.function: Shutdown, active low: pulled low, the output turns off and the part enters its low-power state. It may be driven from 5V logic, or from an open-collector output plus a pull-up resistor sized to cover the gate's leakage (normally several µA) and the SHDN current (1µA typical). Tie it to VIN when shutdown is not used; left floating, the regulator does not run.

pins.name: NC
pins.function: No internal connection. They may be soldered to board copper to help carry heat away.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Supply input. A bypass capacitor of 1µF to 10µF is needed when the part sits more than six inches from the main input filter capacitor, and is worthwhile on battery supplies, whose impedance rises with frequency. The part withstands reverse voltage on IN with respect to GND and OUT: it then blocks as a series diode at the input would, no reverse current flows into it and no reverse voltage reaches the load.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Regulated output to the load. It needs at least 3.3µF of output capacitance to stay stable; loads with large transient steps need more capacitance to hold down the peaks.

pins.name: ADJ
pins.function: Feedback input to the error amplifier on the adjustable version. It regulates at 1.22V with respect to ground, for outputs from 1.22V to 20V. A bias current of 30nA flows into it. It is clamped inside to ±7V.

pins.name: BYP
pins.function: Noise bypass for the internal reference. A capacitor from OUT to BYP lowers output noise; up to 0.01µF may be used, which gives 20µVRMS typical over 10Hz to 100kHz. The pin is clamped inside to ±0.6V (one VBE). Leave it open when no capacitor is fitted.

It may be driven from 5V logic, or from an open-collector output plus a pull-up resistor sized to cover the gate's leakage (normally several µA) and the SHDN current (1µA typical). Tie it to VIN when shutdown is not used; left floating, the regulator does not run.

circuits.title: 3.3V low noise regulator
circuits.description: The LT1962-3.3 runs from a 3.7V to 20V supply and delivers 3.3V at up to 300mA with 20µVRMS of output noise. A 1µF capacitor bypasses the input, SHDN is tied to the input so the regulator is always enabled, SENSE is tied to OUT, a 0.01µF capacitor from OUT to BYP bypasses the reference, and a 10µF capacitor holds the output.

circuits.title: Figure 1. Kelvin sense connection
circuits.description: The output and ground runs to the load each have a trace resistance RP. SENSE is taken straight to the load's positive end, so the regulator holds the voltage at the load instead of at its own OUT pin; GND also connects at the load's return. SHDN is tied to IN. Capacitors sit across the supply and across the load.

notes: Pin numbers: OUT 1, SENSE 2, GND 4, SHDN 5, IN 8.

circuits.title: Figure 2. Adjustable operation
circuits.description: The adjustable LT1962 with a divider from OUT to ground: R2 from OUT to ADJ and R1 from ADJ to ground. The part holds ADJ at 1.22V, so the output is 1.22V × (1 + R2/R1) plus the ADJ bias current times R2. A capacitor holds the output.

parts.note: output capacitor, polarised; no value given

notes: VADJ = 1.22V; IADJ = 30nA at 25°C; output range 1.22V to 20V.
SHDN must be tied to VIN or driven high for the regulator to run.

circuits.title: Adjustable current source
circuits.description: An LT1962-2.5 becomes a current source of 0mA to 300mA into a grounded load. The load current flows through R5 (0.1Ω) in the input line. An LT1004-1.2 reference with R1, R2 and R3 sets a small voltage at the R1 wiper, filtered by R4 and C2, at the op amp's positive input; the negative input sees the IN side of R5 through R6. The op amp (half an LT1490, powered from VIN) drives the SENSE pin, used as FB, with R7 to ground and C3 for compensation, so the regulator output settles where the drop across R5 equals the set voltage. R1 sets the current.

circuits.title: Paralleling of regulators for higher output current
circuits.description: An LT1962-3.3 and an adjustable LT1962 share one 3.3V, 300mA output from an input above 3.7V. Each regulator takes its input through its own 0.1Ω resistor (R1, R2). Half an LT1490 compares the drops across the two resistors through R3 and R4, with C3 as its feedback capacitor, and through R5 trims the ADJ node of the LT1962, whose divider R6/R7 from the output sets it near 3.3V, so the two input currents stay equal. Each regulator has 0.01µF from OUT to BYP. One SHDN line drives both shutdown pins.

operation.text: A 300mA low-dropout linear regulator with 30µA operating quiescent current, under 1µA in shutdown, and about 300mV of dropout at full load. Quiescent current stays controlled in dropout instead of climbing. Fixed versions give 1.5V, 1.8V, 2.5V, 3V, 3.3V and 5V; the adjustable version uses a 1.22V reference. Current limiting, thermal limiting, reverse-battery protection and reverse-current protection are built in, and no external protection diodes are needed.

A capacitor from OUT to BYP bypasses the reference and adds a noise-filtering pole at low frequency; with 0.01µF the output noise falls to 20µVRMS over 10Hz to 100kHz. Choose a low-leakage capacitor of good quality. The bypass capacitor also speeds transient settling: with no bypass capacitor and 10µF at the output, a 10mA to 300mA load step settles to within 1% in under 100µs; with 0.01µF it settles to within 1% in under 10µs, with total deviation below 2%. Start-up time grows with the bypass capacitor, reaching 15ms with CBYP = 0.01µF and COUT = 10µF.

Aluminum electrolytic, tantalum and ceramic output capacitors all work. At least 3.3µF with ESR of 3Ω or less is needed. With 100pF of bypass capacitance 4.7µF is recommended, and with 1000pF or more 6.8µF. The minimum ESR for stability depends on the bypass capacitance (stability curve); the maximum is 3Ω. Larger output capacitance lowers the peak deviation on load steps, and local decoupling capacitors on the powered parts add to the effective output capacitance.

Z5U and Y5V dielectrics pack high capacitance into small cases but lose much of it with DC bias and temperature: a 10µF Y5V part on a 5V output can fall to an effective 1µF to 2µF across temperature. X5R and X7R are steadier and better suited to the output; X7R holds its value better over temperature, X5R costs less and comes in higher values. Some ceramic capacitors are piezoelectric: vibration or thermal stress makes them generate a voltage, which shows up as output noise, especially on the noise-bypass capacitor. On an LT1962-5 with COUT = 10µF, CBYP = 0.01µF and ILOAD = 100mA, a light tap with a pencil on a ceramic capacitor shows as a visible spike on the output (500µV/div, 100ms/div).

Dissipation comes from the load current times the input-output difference plus the GND pin current times the input voltage. Internal thermal limiting protects the part in overloads, but in normal continuous operation the junction must not exceed 125°C. Heat leaves through the board copper; copper stiffeners and plated through-holes help spread it, and nearby heat sources must be counted. Measured junction-to-ambient resistance on a 2500mm² board with 2500mm² of backside copper ranges from 110°C/W to 140°C/W as topside copper shrinks from 2500mm² to 50mm² (Table 1).

IN withstands 20V of reverse voltage. Current into the part is then held below 1mA (typically under 100µA), and no negative voltage appears at the output, so a battery put in backwards harms neither the regulator nor the load.

With IN open or at ground, OUT tolerates being driven to 20V negative. A fixed version then presents roughly 500k or higher and lets less than 40µA flow; the adjustable version passes no current out of OUT. With the input supplied, OUT sources its short-circuit current and thermal limiting protects the part; pulling SHDN low turns it off and stops that current. With the load returned to a negative supply, OUT may sit up to 20V negative and the part still starts and regulates.

ADJ survives being driven to ±7V with respect to ground. With no supply on IN (open or grounded), ADJ driven negative draws no current, and ADJ driven positive behaves as a diode feeding roughly 100k. If a forced-high output could drive ADJ through its divider beyond the 7V clamp, limit the ADJ current to below 5mA.

operation.topic: Backup battery and reverse output current
operation.text: When a backup cell or another supply keeps the output up while the input is grounded, at an intermediate voltage or open, reverse current is blocked, much as a series diode at OUT would block it; the current back into OUT follows the reverse output current curve. With IN forced below OUT, the input current typically drops under 2µA. With OUT above IN, SHDN high or low makes no difference to the reverse output current.

SHDN turns the output on above 2V at most (0.8V typical) and off below 0.25V at least (0.65V typical) over temperature. In shutdown the part draws 0.1µA typical, 1µA maximum, at VIN = 6V. SHDN draws 0.01µA at 0V and 1µA typical at 20V.
